video.title: Could LaMelo Crater Ant's Scoring? Looking At Regression Risks For 26/27

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through the top five and bottom five players in each 9-cat category from last season. His point is that last season's numbers often don't carry over, and he gives last season's leaders as examples. He expects Anthony Edwards, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey to score less, with Ball joining Edwards and Brown sharing the ball with Maxey. He also expects steals leaders like Kevin Porter Jr. to regress. Steals, blocks and free throw percentage change the most from year to year, and lately free throw percentage has changed more than steals. He talks about a possible one-free-throw rule. His view is that more variance in a category makes it easier to punt, because you win it by surprise more often. He warns against reaching for Jalen Brunson in the top 15 and points out that Coby White gives almost nothing in steals and blocks.

rules.text: Don't assume a player repeats last season. Look at several seasons for context before valuing a stat line.
rules.quote: they'll just go, "Well, he he shot 40%." From three, okay, sick. He did, but he shot 32 and 33

rules.text: Free throw percentage and steals are usually the two categories that change the most from year to year.
rules.quote: the two biggest variance categories is free throw percentage and and steals year on year

rules.text: Fantasy is often won on the margins. Small decisions add up.
rules.quote: A lot of it is winning on the margins. In fantasy, it can be that way too.

rules.text: Small changes in counting stats change value a lot. Going from 30 to 28 points loses about 8% of scoring value. Going from 28 to 33 gains about 20%.
rules.quote: you'd go from 30 points a game to 28 points a game, you're losing 8% of your value

rules.text: Two high scorers on the same team rarely both stay top five scorers.
rules.quote: you're playing on the same team, it's almost impossible.

rules.text: A low scorer drafted for other stats hurts points a lot, since the average fantasy scorer puts up about 18 points.
rules.quote: you draft someone scoring five points per game when the average of a scorer in a fantasy league is at 18

rules.text: The baseline for threes has gone up. About two threes a game is now average in fantasy, so the same raw volume is worth less than it used to be.
rules.quote: Now, hitting two threes a game is basically average in a fantasy league. It's a big difference.

rules.text: Non-shooters aren't hurt much in threes because threes are easy to find and stream off waivers.
rules.quote: threes are just readily available off waiver wires. So, you can find two three-pointer per game guys

rules.text: Assists are very hard to find on waivers and are an important category.
rules.quote: assists are incredibly hard to find off the waiverwire and they're a really really important fantasy category

rules.text: Potential assists per 100 possessions can show whether a player has room to gain or lose assists.
rules.quote: I believe the lowest of those players in potential assists was Jokic, meaning there's two ways to look at that.

rules.text: If you draft a low-assist player early, you can fall behind in assists, and big assist guys are rare late in drafts.
rules.quote: You cannot really find many big assist guys later in drafts. Good luck catching up.

rules.text: Steals are very variable and low volume. He weights them down in his rankings and says not to rely on them.
rules.quote: steals get down weighted because when you're looking at them, they are highly variant year on year game by game

rules.text: Expect few of last season's top five steals players to be back in the top five.
rules.quote: don't expect hardly any of them to be back in the top five next season

rules.text: Blocks are very variable from year to year.
rules.quote: much like with steals, blocks are incredibly variable. We have seen this year after year

rules.text: Players with outlier field goal percentages tend to regress, and a small drop can wipe out most of their edge.
rules.quote: you go from outlier good, 100th percentile to 96th percentile, the that advantage you've created is gone

rules.text: Over the last two seasons, free throw percentage has changed more from year to year than steals, because both makes and attempts move around.
rules.quote: The last two seasons has actually been more variable yearon year than steals.

rules.text: Z-scores are standardized against the league, so fewer free throw attempts league-wide wouldn't shrink the gap between top and bottom players.
rules.quote: the idea of standardization, it doesn't mean that if you reduce the amount of attempts by half

rules.text: Punting doesn't mean trying to be the worst. It means ignoring the category.
rules.quote: we remember about punting in category leagues, you are not trying to be bad. You are not trying to be the

rules.text: High-variance categories (steals, blocks, threes, FT%) are better to punt because you still win some by surprise. Stable high-volume categories like points and assists are bad to punt.
rules.quote: Steals, blocks, threes, free throw percentage, higher variance, way more chance to win them, way more success in punting them

rules.text: Use last season's top and bottom lists as a baseline only, not as a reason to fade or buy.
rules.quote: This is not to suggest that the guys at the top of the list you fade or the guys
